findings.explanation: The keep-alive check can keep a frozen maneuver live indefinitely. It checks whether the notification key is still ongoing, then refreshes the age of the cached maneuver without examining the returned notification's post time or contents. If Maps leaves its last notification posted while the rider keeps moving, the watch continues displaying the old arrow and distance and never reaches its 10-second source-age warning. A newer same-key notification whose callback was missed also refreshes the older maneuver. Keep notification presence separate from maneuver freshness, ingest genuinely newer posts returned by the poll, and reconcile the conflicting definitions of `a` in protocol lines 17 and 34.

The service reads state, timestamp and version separately while the verifier can publish from a worker thread. If the verifier clears a vanished source between the state and timestamp reads, `offer` receives the old maneuver with the fresh IDLE timestamp. A heartbeat due on that tick can briefly revive guidance that the watch had already hidden. Publish and consume one immutable snapshot containing all three values.

The parser joins the maneuver and ETA into one string before extracting the street and turn distance. The test's `Turn left onto Nguyễn Trãi` plus `Arrive 14:30` produces `Nguyễn Trãi. Arrive 14:30` as the street. When the ETA changes, Throttle assigns a new step ID and can repeat the turn alert. If the secondary summary also contains a trip distance, that number can become `d` before the dedicated shortCriticalText fallback runs. Parse the ETA and trip summary separately and assert that ETA changes preserve the street and step ID.

The round-four leading-road fix treats the first period, comma or semicolon as the start of a maneuver clause. With `100 m` and `On Dr. Left Fork Road`, the period in `Dr.` exposes `Left Fork Road` to the standalone `left` rule, yielding a left-turn arrow and vibration from the road name. Require an explicit maneuver in the trailing clause before removing the road context.

The parser intentionally suppresses ambiguous directions, but the listener treats that result the same as missing direction text. A navigation-category `200 m` notification saying `Turn left or right` can produce a turn and vibration if its large icon classifies as one direction. Preserve the ambiguity result through the parser boundary and allow icon fallback only when the text supplies no direction.

A determinate ProgressStyle does not establish metre units. Android defaults the scale to 100 when segments are omitted, so a recognized Maps notification using a percentage scale at progress 35 would display 65 m remaining. This affects `r`; progress does not feed the vibration distance `d`. Gate the subtraction on evidence for the captured metre-based format and leave `r=-1` when the scale is unverified. [Android ProgressStyle source](https://android.googlesource.com/platform/frameworks/base/+/refs/heads/android16-qpr2-release/core/java/android/app/Notification.java#13216)

Once two peers are on the skip list, the retry path always keeps the first skipped result. In a mocked scan, B failed first, A failed once and then recovered, and repeated batches ordered `[B, A]` produced attempts `B, A, B, B, B`. The watch never returned to the recovered phone. Rotate eligible skipped peers by least recent attempt while keeping the preference for untried peers.

`Turn left in - 30 m` bypasses the signed-distance rejection because the hyphen has spaces on both sides and follows the word `in`. It becomes a valid-looking 30 m turn and can trigger the urgent alert. Limit the dash exception to a complete maneuver followed by a separator and a bare distance so the tested `Turn right – 100 m` format still works.

A stalled link after an accepted idle frame stays on the waiting screen even after the 3-second receive deadline. A Node probe confirmed that `isStale` is true while `view` still reports `waiting`. The transport watchdog eventually shows the loss state at about eight seconds. Check staleness before rendering an accepted idle frame and keep the idle path silent.

The notification stop action calls `stopSelf()` while `active` remains true until `onDestroy`. A BLE retry already queued on the main handler can reopen GATT between those callbacks. Mark the service inactive and cancel its pending retry when handling the stop action.

The skip-preference test counts connections, so choosing the same failed address in every batch still satisfies its assertions. The pin-rotation test at line 528 also accepts a complete stall because `undefined` differs from the first filter string. Record the target address in the mock and assert the expected peers and the actual second scan variant.

limits: Reviewed the current source, tests, protocol and named prior findings. The checkout advanced to 305ad68 during inspection and ended clean. The available history does not isolate an exact post-round-four snapshot, so findings describe current behavior without attributing each issue to Gemini. The shared default pairing token was treated as the accepted exception.

Read-only Node probes reproduced skipped-peer starvation and the idle timeout discrepancy. A probe using the actual page script with debug status off confirmed that effective-age staleness hides the arrow and starts one loss pulse. A later stale heartbeat and disconnect left that pulse running.

Phone findings are based on source inspection. The reported 51 watch and 41 phone tests and hardware observations came from the handoff. I did not rerun the full suites or verify behavior on a device. The parser fixture tests decoded values and does not establish how the listener handles raw notification extras or whether other Maps notification formats use the same progress units.
Inspection found no raw notification text in the reviewed logging paths. Watch visual layout, arrow assets, wrist-down behavior and native callback timing were not verified.
